problem.title: Law firms can't paste client data into cloud AI
problem.lede: Cloud assistants are fast, but privileged matter data and unsourced answers are risks a practice cannot absorb.

cards.title: Client confidentiality
cards.body: Pasting privileged matter data into a cloud AI service creates privilege and GDPR exposure that cannot be undone.

cards.title: Uncited output is unusable
cards.body: A hallucinated citation cannot support legal advice — an unsourced finding is worse than no finding at all.

cards.title: Automation without accountability
cards.body: No audit trail and no human sign-off means nobody can stand behind the result when it is questioned.

how.title: From transcript to signed-off analysis
how.lede: Three steps, all on your machine.

steps.title: Index the matter
steps.body: The contract is chunked and embedded locally, then stored in Qdrant — no text ever leaves the machine.

steps.title: Analyze the transcript
steps.body: Mithra extracts obligations, risks, and action items, attaches verbatim dual citations, and flags discrepancies.

steps.title: Attorney decides
steps.body: Every AI redline requires an explicit approve or reject — each decision is stamped into the audit trail.

features.title: Built for privileged work
features.lede: Everything needed to turn a meeting into a defensible, cited analysis.

cards.title: Multi-format upload
cards.body: PDF, DOCX, TXT, and Markdown — or paste text directly.

cards.title: Obligations & risks
cards.body: Extracted from the client's perspective, each with a risk level.

cards.title: Verbatim dual citations
cards.body: Quotes from the transcript and the indexed contract, with discrepancy flags when they differ.

cards.title: Human-in-the-loop redlining
cards.body: The model proposes; nothing is applied until the attorney approves or rejects it.

cards.title: Matter-owner attribution
cards.body: No daily tokens or logins — every action is attributed to the matter owner.

cards.title: Tamper-evident audit trail
cards.body: A hash-chained record of every action, verifiable after the fact.

cards.title: Professional PDF reports
cards.body: Export the analysis and the redline review as a clean PDF report.

cards.title: Citation validation
cards.body: Sources are checked against real document IDs — invented citations are refused.

architecture.title: One bounded box. Nothing leaves it.
architecture.lede: Every service runs inside a single local Docker Compose boundary.
architecture.diagramTitle: Mithra runs entirely on your machine
architecture.diagramDesc: A diagram of the local stack. A browser or API client calls a FastAPI service. FastAPI talks to Ollama for language and embedding models, Qdrant for vector search, PostgreSQL for relational data, Redis for queues, and MinIO for object storage. All of these run inside one boundary labelled “Your machine — Docker Compose”. Outside the boundary a crossed-out cloud is labelled “no cloud calls”.
notes: Model swappable with one config line.
Hash-chained audit trail for every action.
Citation validation against real document IDs.

privacy.title: Privacy by architecture, not by policy

gdpr.title: GDPR alignment
gdpr.body: Because processing happens locally, there is no third-country transfer and data minimization is enforced by the architecture itself. Mithra supports your compliance work — it does not replace it.

aiAct.title: EU AI Act alignment
aiAct.body: Human-in-the-loop by design, transparent citations for every finding, and a complete audit trail. The attorney always makes the final call.

privacy.notLegalAdvice: This website is not legal advice.

site.title: How this site respects your privacy
lines: No analytics, no cookies, no trackers.
System fonts only — zero external requests.
Verify it yourself: open DevTools → Network and reload.

about.title: Why the name Mithra
about.brandStory: Mithra — an ancient Persian word meaning 'covenant': a promise made, witnessed, and kept. It is one of the oldest words in the Persian language and the oldest idea in law. We named this tool after that idea — every agreement deserves to be read as if its promise matters.
about.dedication: Dedicated to the memory of my father, Sohrab.
